newsitem.title: USA: U.S. wants Lockerbie bombing suspects put on trial.
newsitem.headline: U.S. wants Lockerbie bombing suspects put on trial.

text.p: Attorney General Janet Reno on Thursday sought to reassure the families of those who died in the 1988 Pan Am bombing over Lockerbie, Scotland, that the United States still wants to bring the perpetrators to trial.

"The American government is committed to the criminal prosecution of those responsible for the murders of 270 victims of the Pam Am Flight 103 bombing," she said in a statement read at her weekly Justice Department news briefing.

"This commitment has not, and it will not, lessen with the passage of time," Reno said. "The Libyan government needs to finally comprehend that the criminal charges ... are not going to simply go away."

She was responding to a letter sent in June by the Libyan Mission to the United Nations to the family members recommending that the two Libyan suspects charged in the bombing be tried in a neutral country.
The letter claimed the U.S. government no longer was interested in the incident, which Reno rejected as untrue and "patently offensive."
She said Libya must hand over the two suspects for trial in the United States or Britain.

In addition, "Libya must disclose all it knows of this crime, pay appropriate compensation and commit to concretely and definitively cease all forms of terrorist action and all assistance to terrorist groups," Reno said.
Reno learned about the letter from families of the victims.
Reno offered no specifics on how the United States would get the Libyans, but told reporters, "What we try to do is consider all possible alternatives, and one thing we do is we don't give up."
